summary.headline: Navneet FY26 revenue fell 3% to INR1,683 crore; management guides FY27 publication growth of about 15% and stationery growth of about 15%, with margins to recover to around 9% after brand spend.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR394 crore versus INR389 crore, while FY26 revenue declined to INR1,683 crore from INR1,733 crore on US tariff disruption and weaker export pricing. Domestic stationery grew 4% in value to INR366 crore on 6% volume growth, but margins were hit by GST exemption on paper stationery (blocking input tax credit) and falling paper prices passed on to customers. Management is shifting to a two-year brand-building push (about INR30 crore in FY27 and INR40-odd crore in FY28) and expects a state curriculum cycle in Maharashtra and Gujarat from FY27. Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary) posted INR42 crore sales and a INR16 crore loss, and is to be merged into Navneet.

segments.name: Publication (state boards)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR719 crore, stable. Management expects a curriculum change in Maharashtra and Gujarat over FY27-FY29 and about 15% growth in a single year; FY27 publication EBIT margin guided at least 200 bps above FY26.

segments.name: Domestic stationery (YOUVA brand)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR366 crore, +4% value on +6% volume. Management guides about 15% growth in FY27 and a normalised EBITDA margin of about 9% in FY27 (post brand spend), against about 13% historically.

segments.name: Export stationery
segments.commentary: Revenue down 10% in FY26 on US tariffs; divisional EBITDA margin down about 3 pp; a 4% favourable FX cushion was passed through as price cuts. Management guides single-digit to higher single-digit growth (8-9%) for FY27 and says no cancellations have been received.

segments.name: Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Sales fell to INR42 crore from INR55 crore with a INR16 crore PAT loss, due to stopped new category creation and higher returns. Merger into Navneet is pending regulatory approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic stationery revenue growth about 15%; subsequent year higher.
FY27 export stationery growth guided at 8-9%, conservative; long-term export growth about 15% possible in normal conditions.
Publication revenue growth of about 15% in a single year during the FY27-FY29 curriculum change; FY27 publication margin at least 200 bps above FY26.
Stationery EBITDA margin about 9% in FY27 post brand spend, and 9.5-10% in the following year, versus about 13% normally. Full-year margin impact from export price cuts expected to be under 100 bps.
Brand spend of about INR30 crore in FY27 and about INR40 crore in FY28; no price premium expected to offset it.

Capex: UAE manufacturing project on hold, so limited spend; India capex about INR25-30 crore in FY27. Southern Gujarat plant cost INR65 crore including land; asset turn 1x in year one, at least 2x in year two, about 2.5x thereafter.
capex_capacity: Southern Gujarat plant: INR65 crore invested including land; mainly plastic-based products for domestic and export markets; plastic export products currently outsourced will move in-house.
Paper capacity utilisation about 80% annually (three months of very low volume due to seasonality); outsourcing used heavily.
Non-paper categories to be initially outsourced under the brand and packaging, with capex deferred category by category.
UAE manufacturing project placed on hold due to geopolitical tensions; very limited investment made so far; may resume depending on the situation.
India capex in FY27 expected at only about INR25-30 crore, with no major land, building or machinery plans.
demand_pricing: Export orders: management says there are no cancellations; back-to-school volumes were finalised Nov-Feb. Price cuts given during the tariff period are being reversed.
Domestic: 6% volume growth achieved despite falling paper prices and price competition from unorganised regional players, which forced price cuts.
Paper prices rose about 8% from the lowest level in the last year; management doubts mills can raise prices for at least the next 3-4 months.

Publication: no curriculum change in Maharashtra/Gujarat since FY18 explained flat revenue; shift of customers to central board and lower per-customer spend also cited. Secondhand book market and trade inventory disappear with curriculum change.
Inflation in developed markets, including the US, is a risk to export buyers; management is haircutting growth by 5-7% for conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: Are export customers cancelling or cutting volumes, and will margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: No cancellations; volumes intact. Price cuts are reversed; only the first two months were affected, so full-year margin impact is under 100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why the shift to aggressive domestic branding, and what is the spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-paper categories need brand awareness to scale quickly. About INR30 crore in year one and about INR40 crore in year two, under the YOUVA brand; no price premium expected.

qa_highlights.question: What are the South Gujarat plant economics?
qa_highlights.answer: INR65 crore invested including land. Asset turn 1x in year one, 2x in year two, about 2.5x thereafter; beyond that, more machinery is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did publication margin fall in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal buying shifts between halves, inflation with no revenue growth, and a leave-encashment provision under the new labour code. Paper prices were favourable in H1 and not in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indiannica revenue decline, and is it being merged?
qa_highlights.answer: Stopped creating new categories and higher returns reduced sales to INR42 crore. Merger into Navneet is planned to cut duplicate costs and share distribution; awaiting approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for a demerger or buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger plans, since the stationery numbers are not large enough. On buyback, management said about three buybacks have been done in the last five years and they may revisit at the right time.

risks_watch: US tariffs and inflation affecting export pricing and buyer demand; FY27 export guidance is only 8-9%.
Execution of the two-year brand spend (INR30 crore then INR40 crore) with no price premium, so it hits margins directly.
Paper price volatility: the 8% rise is seen as temporary, and GST changes on paper stationery.
Timing of the Maharashtra and Gujarat curriculum change and whether publication growth reaches about 15%.
Indiannica merger approvals, integration and losses; CBSE penetration is still an open question for analysts.
UAE project on hold; capex and asset turn at the Gujarat plant depend on export volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term publication and curriculum story, but cautious and sometimes defensive on exports, margins and CBSE. Management openly accepts near-term margin pressure and gives specific FY27 figures, while leaving export growth and some CBSE questions unquantified.
key_quotes: So while these strategic investments will impact on our domestic margins in the short to medium term, they are absolutely vital to secure long-term market dominance.
So in the first year, we have planned around INR30 crores the brand expense. And in the subsequent year, around INR40-odd crores to spend on brand.
So that is a short-term benefit at times we have got in earlier years.
So altogether, we have invested INR65 crores, including buying of a land.

adds.what: Southern Gujarat plant (mainly plastic-based products for domestic and export markets), INR65 crore invested including land

growth.why: Management guides FY27 domestic stationery and publication growth of about 15% and export growth of 8-9%, backed by a 6% domestic volume gain, no export cancellations and a state curriculum change in Maharashtra and Gujarat, but no specific new capacity or order book numbers were given; India capex is only INR25-30 crore and the UAE project is on hold.
